questions.stem: A technician is upgrading the system memory in a laptop. Which RAM form factor is designed for the laptop's smaller footprint?

explanation.correct: SO-DIMM (Small Outline DIMM) is the short, compact memory module built for the limited space inside laptops and small-form-factor PCs.

distractors.B: DIP is an individual chip package soldered to a board, not a user-replaceable module.
distractors.C: A full-size DIMM is the longer desktop/server module; it won't fit a laptop slot.
distractors.D: SIMM is a legacy 30/72-pin module from the 1990s, long replaced by DIMM/SO-DIMM.

explanation.exam_pattern: Laptop RAM = SO-DIMM; desktop/server RAM = full-size DIMM.

questions.stem: A laptop panel is advertised as low cost with very fast response times, but reviewers note washed-out colors and poor viewing angles. Which panel technology is it MOST likely using?

explanation.correct: TN panels are the cheapest and fastest LCDs, but they have narrow viewing angles and weaker color reproduction — exactly the described trade-off.

distractors.A: OLED lights each pixel individually, giving true blacks and excellent color/angles.
distractors.B: VA sits between TN and IPS, offering high contrast rather than washed-out color.
distractors.C: IPS is known for wide viewing angles and accurate color, the opposite of this panel.

explanation.exam_pattern: TN = cheap + fast + poor angles; IPS = best color/angles; OLED = per-pixel, true black.

questions.stem: A laptop has a single small, reversible port that can transfer data, charge the system, and output video using DisplayPort Alternate Mode. Which connector is this?

explanation.correct: USB-C is reversible and carries USB data, USB Power Delivery charging, and video via DisplayPort Alt Mode — one connector for all three.

distractors.A: Lightning is Apple's proprietary reversible connector; it is not the DisplayPort Alt Mode standard.
distractors.B: Mini-USB is a legacy non-reversible connector for data/charging on older peripherals.
distractors.C: Micro-USB is an older, non-reversible connector used mainly for charging/data, not video.

explanation.exam_pattern: USB-C = reversible, does data + Power Delivery + DisplayPort Alt Mode video.

questions.stem: A user taps their smartphone against a store's payment terminal to pay. Which short-range wireless technology enables this contactless transaction?

explanation.correct: NFC (Near Field Communication) works only at a few centimeters, which is what makes tap-to-pay and tap-to-pair secure and intentional.

distractors.A: Wi-Fi Direct links two devices for networking/file transfer, not contactless payment.
distractors.B: Bluetooth reaches roughly 10 m and is used for audio/peripherals, not tap-to-pay.
distractors.C: Infrared needs direct line of sight and is essentially obsolete on modern phones.

explanation.exam_pattern: Tap-to-pay at ~4 cm = NFC; peripherals/audio at ~10 m = Bluetooth.

questions.stem: An administrator wants corporate email, contacts, and calendar to synchronize two-way and wirelessly between the mail server and employees' phones. Which protocol is purpose-built for this?

explanation.correct: Exchange ActiveSync (EAS) pushes and two-way syncs mail, contacts, and calendar to mobile devices, which is exactly what corporate mobile mail needs.

distractors.A: SMTP only sends/relays outbound mail; it does not sync mailboxes, contacts, or calendars.
distractors.B: POP3 only downloads mail to one device (often deleting it from the server) and syncs no calendar/contacts.
distractors.D: FTP transfers files between hosts and has nothing to do with mail synchronization.

explanation.exam_pattern: Two-way push of mail + contacts + calendar to mobile = Exchange ActiveSync; POP3 = download mail only.

questions.stem: After a technician replaces a laptop's LCD panel, Wi-Fi reception becomes very weak even though it was strong before the repair. What is the MOST likely cause?

options.text: The Wi-Fi antenna leads that route through the display lid were not reconnected to the wireless card
The SSD was reseated in the wrong M.2 slot
The system RAM is beginning to fail

explanation.correct: Laptop Wi-Fi antennas sit in the display bezel/lid, with thin leads routed through the hinge to the wireless NIC. Leaving them unplugged after a screen swap cripples reception.

distractors.A: An overheating CPU causes throttling or shutdowns, not a selective loss of Wi-Fi range.
distractors.C: A misplaced SSD would cause boot/storage problems, not specifically weak Wi-Fi.
distractors.D: Failing RAM causes crashes or no-POST symptoms, not a drop in wireless signal strength.

explanation.exam_pattern: Weak Wi-Fi right after a screen/lid repair → reconnect the antenna leads routed through the display.

questions.stem: A web administrator is writing a firewall rule to permit secure (encrypted) web traffic. Which TCP port must the rule allow?

explanation.correct: HTTPS (HTTP over TLS) uses TCP port 443 for encrypted web traffic.

distractors.A: TCP 22 is SSH, used for secure remote command-line access, not web browsing.
distractors.B: TCP 3389 is RDP, used for remote desktop sessions, not web traffic.
distractors.C: TCP 80 is plain HTTP — unencrypted web traffic, not the secure version.

explanation.exam_pattern: HTTPS = 443, HTTP = 80, SSH = 22, RDP = 3389.

questions.stem: A small office needs a device that connects its internal LAN to the ISP and forwards traffic between the LAN and the internet based on IP addresses. Which device does this?

explanation.correct: A router operates at Layer 3 and forwards packets between different networks (LAN ↔ internet) using IP addressing.

distractors.A: A media converter only changes the physical medium (e.g., copper to fiber); it does not route.
distractors.B: A switch forwards frames within a single LAN using MAC addresses; it doesn't route between networks.
distractors.C: A hub is a Layer 1 repeater that blindly copies signals to all ports; it makes no forwarding decisions.

explanation.exam_pattern: Between networks by IP = router (L3); within a LAN by MAC = switch (L2).

questions.stem: A user in a far bedroom gets a weak signal on the 5 GHz band. Moving the connection to which band will generally improve range and wall penetration, at the cost of speed?

explanation.correct: 2.4 GHz uses longer wavelengths that travel farther and pass through walls better than 5 GHz, though it is slower and more congested.

distractors.A: 60 GHz (WiGig/802.11ad) is extremely high speed but only works across a room with line of sight.
distractors.B: The 900 MHz band is used by some cordless phones/IoT, not by standard client Wi-Fi.
distractors.C: 6 GHz (Wi-Fi 6E) offers more bandwidth but has even shorter range and weaker penetration than 5 GHz.

explanation.exam_pattern: 2.4 GHz = farther + slower + crowded; 5/6 GHz = faster + shorter range.

questions.stem: A workstation can reach websites when the user types their IP address directly, but not when the user types the domain name. Which network service is MOST likely at fault?

explanation.correct: DNS resolves domain names to IP addresses. If it fails, raw IP access still works while name-based access breaks — exactly the symptom described.

distractors.A: SMTP sends email; it is unrelated to resolving or reaching web addresses.
distractors.B: NTP synchronizes clocks; it has no role in reaching websites.
distractors.C: DHCP assigns IP configuration; the host clearly already has working IP connectivity.

explanation.exam_pattern: Reachable by IP but not by name → DNS problem.

questions.stem: A residential ISP delivers internet over the same coaxial line used for cable TV, using the DOCSIS standard and a cable modem. Which internet connection type is this?

explanation.correct: Cable internet runs over coaxial TV cabling and uses the DOCSIS standard through a cable modem.

distractors.A: DSL delivers internet over existing twisted-pair telephone lines, not coax.
distractors.C: Satellite uses a dish for a wireless uplink to an orbiting satellite, with high latency.
distractors.D: Fiber to the home uses optical glass strands and an ONT, not coax/DOCSIS.

explanation.exam_pattern: Coax + DOCSIS + cable modem = cable internet; phone line = DSL; glass = fiber.

questions.stem: A technician is documenting default port-to-protocol mappings on a SOHO firewall. Which TWO pairings are correct? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: RDP uses TCP 3389 and DNS uses UDP (and TCP) 53 — both pairings are correct.

distractors.B: TCP 25 is SMTP (outbound mail), not DNS. DNS is port 53.
distractors.C: TCP 23 is Telnet (unencrypted remote CLI), not HTTPS. HTTPS is TCP 443.

explanation.exam_pattern: RDP 3389, DNS 53, SMTP 25, Telnet 23, HTTPS 443.

questions.stem: A technician is terminating a Cat 6 cable to connect a desktop to a Gigabit Ethernet wall jack. Which connector belongs on the cable end?

explanation.correct: RJ45 is the 8-position (8P8C) modular connector used for twisted-pair Ethernet such as Cat 5e/6.

distractors.B: BNC is a bayonet-style connector for coaxial cable (legacy 10BASE2 / video).
distractors.C: LC is a small form-factor fiber-optic connector, used with glass cabling, not copper Ethernet.
distractors.D: RJ11 is the smaller 6-position connector used for analog telephone lines.

explanation.exam_pattern: Twisted-pair Ethernet = RJ45 (8P8C); telephone = RJ11; fiber = LC/SC.

questions.stem: A server administrator specifies ECC memory for a new database server. What is the PRIMARY benefit of ECC RAM?

options.text: It eliminates the need for a page file / virtual memory
It detects and corrects single-bit memory errors to protect data integrity
It always runs at a much higher clock speed than non-ECC RAM
It lets the CPU be overclocked safely

explanation.correct: ECC (Error-Correcting Code) RAM adds parity bits that detect and correct single-bit errors, which matters most on servers where silent data corruption is unacceptable.

distractors.A: A page file is an OS feature; ECC does not remove the need for virtual memory.
distractors.C: ECC is about reliability, not speed; it often runs slightly slower than comparable non-ECC RAM.
distractors.D: ECC has nothing to do with CPU overclocking headroom.

explanation.exam_pattern: ECC = error detection/correction for servers; it is a reliability feature, not a speed feature.

questions.stem: A user wants the fastest possible boot and application drive. Which option delivers the HIGHEST sequential throughput?

options.text: An M.2 NVMe SSD connected over the PCIe bus

explanation.correct: NVMe SSDs communicate over the high-bandwidth PCIe bus, far exceeding SATA's limits and crushing any mechanical drive on throughput and latency.

distractors.B: A 5,400 RPM HDD is slower still, common in budget laptops and external drives.
distractors.C: A SATA SSD is fast but capped by the SATA III interface at about 6 Gb/s (~550 MB/s).
distractors.D: A 7,200 RPM HDD has spinning platters and heads; it is far slower than any SSD.

explanation.exam_pattern: Speed order: NVMe (PCIe/M.2) > SATA SSD > HDD; SATA III caps near 6 Gb/s.

questions.stem: A customer is building a compact home-theater PC and wants the SMALLEST of the standard ATX-family motherboard form factors. Which should they choose?

explanation.correct: Mini-ITX (170 x 170 mm) is the smallest common form factor, typically with a single expansion slot — ideal for a small HTPC build.

distractors.B: MicroATX is larger than Mini-ITX, with more expansion slots.
distractors.C: Full ATX is the standard desktop size, larger than MicroATX.
distractors.D: E-ATX is the largest, used for high-end workstation and server boards.

explanation.exam_pattern: Size small → large: Mini-ITX < MicroATX < ATX < E-ATX.

questions.stem: A technician reads '80 PLUS Gold' on a power supply's label. What does this rating describe?

options.text: The maximum wattage the PSU can supply
The number of SATA power connectors included
The physical dimensions of the PSU
The PSU's energy efficiency — how much drawn AC power is delivered as usable DC

explanation.correct: 80 PLUS tiers (White, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Titanium) rate efficiency — the percentage of AC input converted to DC output rather than wasted as heat.

distractors.A: Maximum wattage is a separate spec printed elsewhere on the label (e.g., 650 W).
distractors.B: Connector count is a separate detail and is not what the 80 PLUS badge measures.
distractors.C: Physical size (e.g., ATX vs SFX) is unrelated to the efficiency certification.

explanation.exam_pattern: 80 PLUS = efficiency tier; wattage is a separate rating entirely.

questions.stem: In the laser printer imaging process, which step comes IMMEDIATELY AFTER exposing, the stage where the laser writes the latent image onto the photosensitive drum?

explanation.correct: The sequence is processing, charging, exposing, developing, transferring, fusing, cleaning. After exposing writes the latent image, developing coats that image with toner.

distractors.A: Fusing bonds toner to the paper with heat and pressure near the END of the process.
distractors.B: Cleaning wipes residual toner and charge from the drum as the final step.
distractors.D: Charging applies a uniform charge to the drum and happens BEFORE exposing, not after.

explanation.exam_pattern: Laser 7 steps: Processing, Charging, Exposing, Developing, Transferring, Fusing, Cleaning.

questions.stem: An administrator wants to control three rack servers from a single keyboard, monitor, and mouse, switching between them with the press of a button. Which device provides this?

explanation.correct: A KVM (Keyboard, Video, Mouse) switch shares one set of peripherals across multiple computers, toggling control between them.

distractors.A: A USB hub only adds extra USB ports to one computer; it doesn't switch between machines.
distractors.C: A docking station expands a single laptop's connectivity, not control of several servers.
distractors.D: A network switch connects devices on a LAN; it has nothing to do with sharing peripherals.

explanation.exam_pattern: One keyboard/monitor/mouse controlling many PCs = KVM switch.

questions.stem: A technician must pick a RAID level for a server that has to keep running if a single drive fails. Which TWO of the following RAID levels provide fault tolerance? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: RAID 1 mirrors identical copies across drives, and RAID 5 stripes data with distributed parity; both can survive the loss of a single drive.

distractors.A: JBOD simply concatenates disks with no parity or mirroring, so it offers no fault tolerance.
distractors.B: RAID 0 stripes for speed/capacity with NO redundancy — losing any one drive loses the whole array.

explanation.exam_pattern: Fault tolerant: RAID 1 (mirror), 5 (parity), 10 (mirror+stripe). RAID 0 = speed only, NO redundancy.

questions.stem: A company uses a web-based office suite where the provider manages the servers, operating system, and the applications, and users just sign in through a browser. Which cloud service model is this?

explanation.correct: SaaS delivers finished applications over the web (webmail, online office suites); the provider runs and maintains every layer beneath the app.

distractors.B: An on-premises datacenter is not a cloud service model at all.
distractors.C: PaaS provides a development platform (runtime, OS, tools) for building apps, not a finished app.
distractors.D: IaaS provides raw compute, storage, and networking (VMs) that the customer configures and manages.

explanation.exam_pattern: SaaS = finished app; PaaS = dev platform; IaaS = raw VMs/infrastructure.

questions.stem: An organization keeps sensitive records on its own private cloud but 'bursts' to a public cloud provider during peak demand. Which cloud DEPLOYMENT model is this?

explanation.correct: A hybrid cloud combines private and public clouds so workloads can move between them — cloud bursting to public capacity at peak is a textbook example.

distractors.A: A private cloud alone is dedicated to one organization with no public component.
distractors.B: A community cloud is shared by several organizations with common requirements, not this scenario.
distractors.D: A public cloud alone is fully provider-owned and shared; it isn't the mix described.

explanation.exam_pattern: Private + public working together = hybrid; shared by several orgs = community.

questions.stem: A retailer's cloud platform automatically scales server capacity UP during a holiday spike and back DOWN afterward, appearing to offer unlimited resources on demand. Which essential cloud characteristic BEST describes this?

explanation.correct: Rapid elasticity is the ability to scale resources out and back in quickly — often automatically — to match changing demand.

distractors.A: Resource pooling is the provider serving many tenants from a shared pool of hardware.
distractors.B: Broad network access means the service is reachable over standard networks and devices.
distractors.C: Measured service is the metered, pay-per-use billing of what you consume, not the scaling itself.

explanation.exam_pattern: Scale up/down on demand = rapid elasticity; metered pay-per-use = measured service.

questions.stem: A developer installs VirtualBox on top of their existing Windows 11 desktop to run several test virtual machines. Which TYPE of hypervisor is this?

explanation.correct: A Type 2 (hosted) hypervisor runs as an application ON TOP of an existing host OS — VirtualBox and VMware Workstation on Windows are classic examples.

distractors.A: A container engine shares the host kernel to run isolated apps, not full virtual machines.
distractors.B: An emulator translates a different CPU architecture; a hosted hypervisor runs same-architecture VMs natively.
distractors.D: A Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisor installs directly on the hardware with no host OS (e.g., ESXi, Hyper-V).

explanation.exam_pattern: Type 2 = runs on a host OS (VirtualBox); Type 1 = bare metal on the hardware (ESXi).

questions.stem: A technician plans to run four virtual machines at the same time on one workstation for testing. Which hardware resource is MOST important to have in sufficient quantity?

options.text: System RAM to allocate to each VM

explanation.correct: Every running VM is assigned its own memory (along with CPU cores and disk), so ample system RAM is the key resource that limits how many VMs can run at once.

distractors.A: USB port count does not determine VM capacity.
distractors.C: Optical-drive speed is irrelevant to running VMs, which boot from virtual disks.
distractors.D: Display resolution affects what you see, not how many VMs the host can keep in memory.

explanation.exam_pattern: More simultaneous VMs → more RAM and CPU cores (plus virtualization enabled in BIOS/UEFI).

questions.stem: A technician has just tested and CONFIRMED a theory about why a PC won't boot. According to the CompTIA six-step troubleshooting methodology, what is the NEXT step?

options.text: Establish a theory of probable cause
Document the findings, actions, and outcomes
Establish a plan of action to resolve the problem and implement the solution

explanation.correct: Once the theory is tested and confirmed (step 3), step 4 is to establish a plan of action and implement the fix.

distractors.A: Establishing a theory is step 2, which precedes testing the theory.
distractors.B: Identifying the problem is step 1 and has already happened.
distractors.C: Documenting findings/actions/outcomes is the final step (step 6), after verification.

explanation.exam_pattern: 6 steps: Identify → Theory → Test theory → Plan & implement → Verify (+prevent) → Document.

questions.stem: A desktop powers on — fans spin and lights come on — but there is no video output and the motherboard emits a repeating POST beep code. Which component should the technician suspect FIRST?

options.text: Memory (RAM) that has failed or is not seated correctly

explanation.correct: Power present but no video plus POST beep codes classically points to RAM (failed or unseated) or the GPU; reseating/testing memory is the quick, cheap first move.

distractors.A: A weak CMOS battery typically just resets the clock/BIOS settings; it doesn't cause a no-video POST beep pattern.
distractors.B: A bad hard drive still lets the system POST and show video — you'd see a 'no boot device' message instead.
distractors.C: A network cable has no effect on whether the system POSTs or produces video.

explanation.exam_pattern: Fans on, no video, beeping = POST failure → suspect RAM/GPU first; drive faults still POST.

questions.stem: A laptop screen is extremely dim, but you can faintly make out the desktop when you shine a flashlight at an angle on it. An external monitor works fine. What is the MOST likely faulty part?

options.text: The display backlight (or its inverter on older CCFL panels)

explanation.correct: A faint image visible under a flashlight means the LCD is still rendering but not lit — the backlight (or the inverter that powers a CCFL backlight) has failed.

distractors.A: RAM has no role in screen brightness; failing RAM causes crashes or no-POST symptoms.
distractors.B: A driver fault usually produces artifacts, wrong resolution, or no image — not a dim-but-present picture.
distractors.C: The hard drive stores data and does not control the display backlight.

explanation.exam_pattern: Image faintly visible with a flashlight = backlight/inverter failure, not the GPU/driver.

questions.stem: A Windows workstation that normally receives its address automatically now shows an IP of 169.254.12.44 and cannot reach any other host. What does this MOST likely indicate?

options.text: The client could not reach a DHCP server and self-assigned an APIPA address
DNS is misconfigured but DHCP is working normally
The default gateway intentionally hands out 169.254 addresses
The workstation obtained a valid public IP address

explanation.correct: A 169.254.x.x address is APIPA (Automatic Private IP Addressing), which Windows self-assigns ONLY when no DHCP server answers — so the host can't communicate beyond its local link.

distractors.B: The symptom is a failed address assignment (DHCP), not name resolution (DNS).
distractors.C: Gateways/DHCP servers hand out usable addresses; the 169.254 range is a fallback, not a design choice.
distractors.D: 169.254.x.x is a link-local private range, not a routable public address.

explanation.exam_pattern: 169.254.x.x = APIPA → DHCP unreachable/failed; it's a self-assigned link-local address.

questions.stem: Pages from a laser printer come out with toner that smudges and rubs off the paper easily. Which component is MOST likely failing?

explanation.correct: The fuser uses heat and pressure to bond toner permanently to the page. If it fails or can't reach temperature, toner sits loose on the paper and smears.

distractors.B: The network interface affects connectivity, not print quality or toner fusing.
distractors.C: The scanner glass only affects copy/scan quality, not printed toner adhesion.
distractors.D: The paper tray only feeds paper; it doesn't affect whether toner is bonded.

explanation.exam_pattern: Laser toner that smears/rubs off = fuser not bonding toner (the heat-and-pressure stage).

questions.stem: A desktop runs fine when idle but shuts itself off abruptly during intensive gaming. The interior is caked with dust. What is the MOST likely cause?

options.text: The system is overheating and triggering a thermal shutdown

explanation.correct: Abrupt shutdowns only under heavy load, combined with dust blocking airflow, point to overheating — the system powers off to protect the CPU/components.

distractors.A: A corrupt keyboard driver affects input only; it cannot shut the computer down under load.
distractors.B: A loose monitor cable causes no display or flicker, not a full system shutdown.
distractors.C: An unreachable DNS server breaks name resolution; it never powers the machine off.

explanation.exam_pattern: Random shutdowns under load + dust/blocked airflow = overheating / thermal protection.

questions.stem: A technician needs a USB standard capable of 10 Gbps for an external NVMe enclosure. Which USB specification provides this data rate?

explanation.correct: USB 3.2 Gen 2 (formerly USB 3.1 Gen 2, SuperSpeed+) runs at 10 Gbps, enough to approach NVMe speeds over an external enclosure.

distractors.A: USB 2.0 (Hi-Speed) is only 480 Mbps — far too slow for an NVMe enclosure.
distractors.B: USB 3.2 Gen 1 (the old USB 3.0 / 3.1 Gen 1, SuperSpeed) tops out at 5 Gbps.
distractors.C: USB 1.1 (Full-Speed) is a legacy 12 Mbps standard.

explanation.exam_pattern: USB speeds: 2.0 = 480 Mbps, 3.2 Gen 1 = 5 Gbps, 3.2 Gen 2 = 10 Gbps, Gen 2x2 = 20 Gbps.

questions.stem: A workstation user wants ONE cable on the USB-C connector that carries 40 Gbps of data plus video. Which interface meets all of these requirements?

explanation.correct: Thunderbolt 3 (and 4) run at 40 Gbps over the USB-C connector and carry data, video (DisplayPort), and power on a single cable.

distractors.A: USB 3.2 Gen 1 is only 5 Gbps and does not natively carry DisplayPort video on its own.
distractors.C: HDMI 1.4 is a video-only connector (about 10.2 Gbps) and is not a USB-C port.
distractors.D: eSATA carries only the SATA storage signal (about 6 Gbps) — no video and not USB-C.

explanation.exam_pattern: Thunderbolt 3/4 = 40 Gbps over USB-C, carrying data + video + power.

questions.stem: An M.2 SSD has TWO notches on its edge connector (both a B key and an M key). What does this B+M keying indicate?

options.text: It supports PCIe x4 NVMe at full speed
It will physically fit either a B-keyed or an M-keyed M.2 socket
It requires a separate 24-pin power connector
It only works in laptops, never in desktops

explanation.correct: A B+M (two-notch) module uses the pins common to both keys, so it drops into either a B-key or an M-key socket; such modules are SATA or PCIe x2.

distractors.A: Full PCIe x4 NVMe needs an M-key-only module; a B+M module is limited to PCIe x2 or SATA.
distractors.C: M.2 draws power through its edge connector; there is no separate 24-pin feed (that is the ATX board connector).
distractors.D: M.2 sockets appear on both laptops and desktop motherboards.

explanation.exam_pattern: M.2 keys: M-key = up to PCIe x4 (NVMe); B-key = PCIe x2/SATA; B+M (two notches) fits both sockets.

questions.stem: A technician needs a single cable that carries BOTH digital video AND audio from a PC to a display. Which TWO interfaces do this? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: HDMI and DisplayPort both carry digital video and audio over one cable, which is why they are standard on modern GPUs, laptops, and TVs/monitors.

distractors.A: DVI-D carries digital video only — standard DVI does not carry audio.
distractors.D: VGA is an analog, video-only connector (15-pin); it carries no audio and no digital signal.

explanation.exam_pattern: Video + audio on one cable = HDMI / DisplayPort; DVI = video only; VGA = analog video only.

questions.stem: A technician tries to install a DDR4 DIMM into a motherboard with DDR5 slots, but the module will not seat. What is the reason?

options.text: DDR4 needs a higher voltage that physically melts the slot
The notch (key) on a DDR4 module is in a different position than a DDR5 slot's key
A DDR4 module has far more pins than a DDR5 slot can accept
The DDR4 module is physically much longer than the slot

explanation.correct: Each DDR generation is keyed in a different notch position and is not physically or electrically interchangeable, so a DDR4 stick will not seat in a DDR5 slot.

distractors.A: Voltages differ (DDR3 1.5 V, DDR4 1.2 V, DDR5 1.1 V) but a mismatch does not 'melt' the slot; the key simply blocks seating.
distractors.C: DDR4 and DDR5 desktop DIMMs both have 288 pins, so pin count is not the obstacle — the keying position differs.
distractors.D: Full-size desktop DIMMs are the same length across generations; length is not the issue.

explanation.exam_pattern: DDR generations are notch-keyed and NOT interchangeable; voltages: DDR3 1.5 V, DDR4 1.2 V, DDR5 1.1 V.

questions.stem: To get the best memory bandwidth, a technician installs two identical sticks into the color-matched slots (A2 and B2). Which configuration does this create?

explanation.correct: Matched modules in the paired, color-coded slots enable dual-channel mode, widening the path to memory and roughly doubling bandwidth versus one stick.

distractors.A: 'Triple parity' is not a memory channel mode (dual parity is RAID 6, a storage term).
distractors.C: ECC is an error-detection/correction feature of the modules, not a channel configuration.
distractors.D: Single channel uses one module (or populates one channel), giving lower bandwidth.

explanation.exam_pattern: Matched pairs in color-matched slots = dual channel; HEDT/server boards add triple/quad channel.

questions.stem: A Windows PC with little RAM is slow, and the OS is using an area on the storage drive to hold data that overflows physical memory. What is this disk-based area called?

explanation.correct: Virtual memory uses a pagefile on the drive as overflow for physical RAM; heavy paging ('thrashing') slows the system and signals that more RAM is needed.

distractors.A: ReadyBoost uses a USB flash drive as a supplemental cache — not the primary pagefile being described.
distractors.B: Shadow Copy (VSS) takes point-in-time snapshots for restore/backup, not memory overflow.
distractors.C: There is no 'ECC buffer' that extends RAM onto disk; ECC corrects bit errors within RAM.

explanation.exam_pattern: RAM overflow spills to the pagefile on disk = virtual memory; constant paging means add physical RAM.

questions.stem: A server board's documentation calls for 'registered (buffered)' memory. What does the register/buffer on an RDIMM actually do?

options.text: Buffers address/command signals between the modules and the memory controller for stability with many modules
Doubles the rated clock speed of the RAM

explanation.correct: Registered (buffered) DIMMs place a register between the DRAM chips and the controller, reducing electrical load so servers can run many high-capacity modules reliably.

distractors.A: CPU cache (L1/L2/L3) is separate on-die SRAM; buffering does not replace it.
distractors.B: Firmware lives in the BIOS/UEFI flash chip, not on a DIMM's register.
distractors.D: Buffering improves signal integrity and capacity, not clock speed — RDIMMs are often slightly slower.

explanation.exam_pattern: Registered/buffered (RDIMM) = servers (more modules, stability); unbuffered (UDIMM) = desktops.

questions.stem: An older ultrabook holds a compact SSD on a card that carries the SATA signal in a slot predating M.2. Which legacy SSD form factor is this MOST likely?

explanation.correct: mSATA is a small SSD form factor (physically like Mini PCIe) that carries the SATA signal; it was common in ultrabooks before M.2 replaced it.

distractors.A: M.2 NVMe is the newer, faster standard that superseded mSATA and can use the PCIe bus.
distractors.C: eMMC is flash soldered to the board (phones, budget laptops), not a removable SATA card.
distractors.D: 3.5-inch is the desktop hard-drive size, not a compact ultrabook SSD card.

explanation.exam_pattern: mSATA = legacy compact SATA SSD; M.2 = modern (SATA or NVMe/PCIe); eMMC = soldered flash.

questions.stem: A budget laptop drive combines a large spinning platter with a small NAND flash cache to speed up frequently used files in one unit. What is this drive called?

explanation.correct: An SSHD pairs a magnetic HDD with a small SSD cache, accelerating commonly used data while keeping the high capacity and low cost of a spinning drive.

distractors.B: RAID 0 stripes across multiple separate drives; it is not a single hybrid device.
distractors.C: An optical drive reads/writes CDs, DVDs, or Blu-ray discs — not a hybrid storage device.
distractors.D: An NVMe SSD is pure flash on the PCIe bus — no spinning platter.

explanation.exam_pattern: SSHD = HDD platter + small flash cache in one drive (capacity plus some speed).

questions.stem: A database server needs BOTH the speed of striping AND the redundancy of mirroring, and the budget allows at least four drives. Which RAID level BEST fits?

explanation.correct: RAID 10 mirrors pairs of drives and stripes across them, giving both high performance and fault tolerance; it requires a minimum of four drives.

distractors.B: RAID 1 mirrors for redundancy but does not stripe, so it lacks the performance gain.
distractors.C: RAID 0 stripes for speed only, with zero redundancy — one failure loses the whole array.
distractors.D: RAID 5 adds redundancy with single distributed parity but carries a write penalty, so writes are slower than RAID 10.

explanation.exam_pattern: RAID 10 = stripe of mirrors (min 4, speed + redundancy); RAID 5 = striping with single distributed parity (min 3).

questions.stem: A technician must connect an external drive enclosure to a shielded port that uses the SATA protocol and is rated for external cable runs up to about 2 meters. Which port is this?

explanation.correct: eSATA (external SATA) is the externally shielded variant with a sturdier connector rated for longer runs (about 2 m); note that standard eSATA carries data only — no power.

distractors.A: Molex is a legacy 4-pin DC power connector, not a data interface.
distractors.B: RJ11 is a 6-position telephone-line connector, unrelated to storage.
distractors.D: The internal 7-pin SATA data connector is unshielded and intended for inside the case (about 1 m).

explanation.exam_pattern: eSATA = external, shielded, data-only (no power), ~2 m; internal SATA data cable ~1 m.

questions.stem: A technician handles an Intel desktop CPU and sees flat contact pads on its underside, while the delicate pins are in the motherboard socket. Which socket type is this?

explanation.correct: LGA puts the pins in the socket and flat lands/pads on the CPU — the arrangement Intel desktop processors have long used.

distractors.A: SO-DIMM is a laptop RAM form factor, not a CPU socket.
distractors.B: BGA solders the chip permanently to the board (laptops, phones); it is not a swappable socket.
distractors.C: PGA places the pins on the CPU and the holes in the socket (traditionally AMD).

explanation.exam_pattern: LGA = pins on socket (Intel); PGA = pins on CPU (traditional AMD); BGA = soldered.

questions.stem: A technician installs a discrete graphics card. Which expansion slot provides the MOST lanes and is the standard choice for a modern GPU?

explanation.correct: A PCIe x16 slot provides 16 lanes, the highest common bandwidth and the standard slot for a graphics card.

distractors.A: Legacy PCI is an older, slower parallel bus with no 'lanes' and is not used for modern GPUs.
distractors.B: PCIe x4 offers more than x1 but far fewer lanes than x16.
distractors.C: PCIe x1 has a single lane, used for small cards (sound, NIC, capture) — too little bandwidth for a GPU.

explanation.exam_pattern: GPU → PCIe x16; smaller add-in cards → x1/x4; more lanes = more bandwidth.

questions.stem: Every time a desktop is unplugged overnight, it boots with the wrong date/time and loses its saved BIOS/UEFI settings. Which component should be replaced?

explanation.correct: A coin-cell CMOS battery (typically CR2032) keeps the real-time clock and BIOS/UEFI settings alive with no power; losing time/settings points to a dead CMOS battery.

distractors.A: A failed PSU would prevent the system from powering on, not merely reset the clock.
distractors.B: A failing CPU causes crashes or no-boot, not specifically a reset clock.
distractors.C: Bad RAM causes memory errors or no-boot, not loss of date/time settings.

explanation.exam_pattern: Clock resets / BIOS settings lost after power-off = dead CMOS battery (CR2032).

questions.stem: A technician must enable CPU hardware-assisted virtualization in firmware to run a hypervisor efficiently. Which TWO technologies are the CPU virtualization extensions? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: Intel VT-x and AMD-V are the hardware virtualization extensions; enabling them in BIOS/UEFI lets a hypervisor run VMs with hardware acceleration.

distractors.A: TPM 2.0 is a security/crypto module (BitLocker, Windows 11), not a virtualization extension.
distractors.C: Intel SpeedStep is a CPU power/frequency-scaling feature, unrelated to virtualization.

explanation.exam_pattern: Firmware virtualization = Intel VT-x / AMD-V; don't confuse with TPM (security) or SpeedStep (power).

questions.stem: A high-end graphics card needs supplemental power directly from the PSU. Which TWO connectors are the standard PCIe power connectors for a GPU? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: GPUs draw supplemental power through 6-pin and 8-pin (6+2) PCIe power connectors from the power supply.

distractors.C: The 15-pin SATA power connector feeds drives, not a GPU's PCIe power input.
distractors.D: The 24-pin ATX connector powers the motherboard, not the graphics card directly.

explanation.exam_pattern: GPU supplemental power = 6-pin / 8-pin (6+2) PCIe; 24-pin = motherboard; SATA power = drives.

questions.stem: Besides the 24-pin main connector, which connector supplies dedicated power to the CPU near the top of the motherboard?

explanation.correct: The 4-pin or 8-pin EPS connector (often labeled CPU or ATX12V) delivers dedicated 12 V power to the processor's voltage regulators near the top of the board.

distractors.A: A 6-pin PCIe connector supplies graphics cards, not the CPU socket.
distractors.B: A 15-pin SATA power connector feeds storage drives.
distractors.D: A 4-pin Molex is a legacy peripheral/fan power connector, not the CPU power feed.

explanation.exam_pattern: 24-pin = board; 4/8-pin EPS (ATX12V) = CPU; 6/8-pin PCIe = GPU; SATA/Molex = drives.

questions.stem: A technician wants a power supply that lets them attach ONLY the cables a build actually needs, improving airflow and cable management. Which PSU design provides this?

explanation.correct: A fully modular PSU has detachable cables, so only the required cables are connected, reducing clutter and improving airflow.

distractors.A: A non-modular PSU has every cable permanently attached, so unused leads must be tucked away.
distractors.B: Semi-passive/fanless refers to cooling and noise behavior, not detachable cabling.
distractors.D: Dual-rail describes how the 12 V output is split across protected rails, not cable attachment.

explanation.exam_pattern: Modular = detach unused cables; non-modular = fixed cables; semi-modular = some fixed, some detachable.

questions.stem: A PSU has a red slide switch marked '115/230.' What does setting this switch wrong for the region's mains voltage risk?

options.text: Converting the PSU's output from DC back to AC
Component damage or a no-power condition, because it selects the AC input voltage range

explanation.correct: The 115/230 selector matches the PSU to the local mains (about 120 V in North America, about 230 V in Europe). Set to 115 on 230 V mains it can be destroyed; set to 230 on 115 V it usually will not power on.

distractors.A: A PSU converts AC to DC for the PC; this switch does not reverse that.
distractors.B: The switch selects input voltage; it does not alter the 80 PLUS efficiency certification.
distractors.C: Maximum wattage is fixed by the PSU's design, not by the input-voltage switch.

explanation.exam_pattern: 115/230 selector matches mains; wrong setting = damage (115 on 230 V) or no power (230 on 115 V).

questions.stem: An office must scan 50-page documents without placing each sheet on the glass by hand. Which scanner feature should the technician recommend?

explanation.correct: An ADF pulls in a stack of pages and scans them one after another, ideal for multi-page documents; many ADFs also support duplex (two-sided) scanning.

distractors.A: A barcode wand/scanner reads barcodes, not full document pages.
distractors.B: A flatbed-only scanner requires placing each page on the glass individually.
distractors.C: A signature pad captures handwritten signatures, not document pages.

explanation.exam_pattern: Multi-page/batch scanning = ADF; single page, photos, or books = flatbed glass.

questions.stem: A retail checkout needs a device for customers to sign for credit-card purchases electronically. Which peripheral is purpose-built for this?

explanation.correct: A signature pad captures a handwritten signature electronically, commonly at point-of-sale and for signing documents.

distractors.B: A flatbed scanner digitizes pages or photos, not a live signature at checkout.
distractors.C: A KVM switch shares one keyboard/monitor/mouse among multiple PCs.
distractors.D: A webcam captures video/images, not a pen-based signature.

explanation.exam_pattern: Capture a handwritten signature at the point of sale = signature pad.

questions.stem: On a tablet, which component translates the user's finger touches and gestures into input coordinates the operating system can use?

explanation.correct: The digitizer is the touch-sensitive layer over the display that converts physical touch or pen contact into digital coordinates for the OS.

distractors.A: A webcam captures images/video, not touch input.
distractors.B: An inverter supplies high voltage to a CCFL backlight on older LCDs; it does not sense touch.
distractors.C: The backlight illuminates the LCD panel; it produces no input.

explanation.exam_pattern: Touch input layer = digitizer; display output = LCD/backlight; older backlight power = inverter.

questions.stem: A laser printer's output smears when rubbed right after printing. Which step/component is responsible for permanently bonding the toner to the paper?

options.text: Fusing (the fuser assembly's heat and pressure)

explanation.correct: The fusing step uses the fuser's heated rollers and pressure to melt and bond toner to the paper; smearing/unfused toner points to a fuser problem.

distractors.A: Cleaning removes residual toner and charge from the drum at the end of the cycle.
distractors.B: Charging applies a uniform charge to the drum before imaging — not where toner is bonded.
distractors.D: Developing coats the latent image on the drum with toner, before it ever reaches the paper.

explanation.exam_pattern: Toner smears / won't bond = fusing step; order: processing, charging, exposing, developing, transferring, fusing, cleaning.

questions.stem: A warehouse must print on multipart carbon-copy (NCR) forms, where pins physically strike through several sheets at once. Which printer type is required?

explanation.correct: An impact (dot-matrix) printer strikes pins against an inked ribbon and paper, the only common type that can print through multipart carbon/NCR forms.

distractors.A: A direct thermal printer heats special paper and also cannot create carbon copies.
distractors.B: An inkjet sprays ink droplets and cannot press through carbon copies.
distractors.C: A laser printer uses toner and heat and cannot imprint through multipart forms.

explanation.exam_pattern: Multipart/carbon-copy forms = impact (dot-matrix) printer (pins + ribbon).

questions.stem: A maker's 3D printer melts a spool of plastic filament and extrudes it layer by layer through a heated nozzle. Which 3D printing technology is this?

explanation.correct: FDM feeds a thermoplastic filament through a heated nozzle and deposits it layer by layer — the most common consumer 3D printing method.

distractors.A: Toner fusing is a 2D laser-printer process, not a 3D printing technology.
distractors.C: Dye sublimation is a 2D photo-printing method that heats dye onto media.
distractors.D: Resin (SLA) printing cures liquid photopolymer with light; there is no filament spool or heated nozzle.

explanation.exam_pattern: 3D FDM = heated nozzle + filament spool; resin/SLA = UV-cured liquid resin.

questions.stem: A laptop has an empty 2.5-inch SATA bay and an empty M.2 slot wired for PCIe. A technician wants the drive with the HIGHEST sequential throughput. Which option should they install?

explanation.correct: An M.2 NVMe SSD talks over PCIe lanes, so it easily exceeds 2,000-7,000 MB/s and blows past anything on the SATA bus.

distractors.A: A 2.5-inch SATA SSD is fast but capped by the SATA III bus at about 6 Gb/s (~550 MB/s).
distractors.C: An M.2 SATA SSD uses the same small slot but still rides the SATA bus, so it hits the same ~550 MB/s ceiling — M.2 is only the form factor.
distractors.D: A mechanical 7200 RPM hard drive is the slowest choice by far (~100-160 MB/s).

explanation.exam_pattern: M.2 is a form factor, not a speed. NVMe (PCIe) = fastest; SATA (2.5" or M.2) is capped ~6 Gb/s.

questions.stem: A user's laptop no longer sits flat and the trackpad is bulging upward from underneath. What has MOST likely happened, and how should the technician respond?

options.text: The SSD is full; delete files to free space
A SO-DIMM has come loose; reseat the memory modules
The system board warped from heat; replace the motherboard
The lithium-ion battery is swelling; power it down, avoid puncturing it, and replace it with the correct part

explanation.correct: A swelling (puffed) lithium-ion battery expands and pushes the case and trackpad outward. It is a fire/injury hazard: stop using it, do not puncture it, and swap in the correct replacement.

distractors.A: A full SSD slows the system or blocks saves; it cannot deform the case.
distractors.B: A loose SO-DIMM causes no-boot or memory errors, not physical bulging of the chassis.
distractors.C: A warped board is not what lifts the trackpad, and replacing it ignores the obvious swollen battery underneath.

explanation.exam_pattern: Case/trackpad bulging = swollen Li-ion battery. Do not puncture; replace it safely.

questions.stem: While replacing the wireless card in an older laptop, a technician finds a half-size card with a 52-pin edge connector that seats at an angle under two retention clips — it is not an M.2 card. Which interface is this WLAN card using?

explanation.correct: Older laptop Wi-Fi/Bluetooth modules use Mini PCI Express (Mini-PCIe): a small 52-pin card that inserts at an angle and clips down.

distractors.A: Conventional PCI is a legacy desktop expansion bus with long slots, not used for internal laptop WLAN modules.
distractors.B: ExpressCard is a user-accessible slot on the side of a laptop for external add-in cards, not the internal WLAN card interface.
distractors.C: M.2 is the newer, smaller keyed edge-connector standard that replaced Mini-PCIe for WLAN — the stem rules it out.

explanation.exam_pattern: 52-pin angled WLAN card = Mini-PCIe (older); the newer equivalent is a keyed M.2 card.

questions.stem: A company wants staff to unlock their laptops by touch instead of typing a password. Which built-in laptop component provides this?

explanation.correct: A fingerprint reader is a biometric scanner that authenticates the user from a body characteristic — a touch instead of a typed password.

distractors.A: A TPM securely stores encryption keys and measurements; it does not read fingerprints.
distractors.B: An NFC sensor handles contactless tap (pay/pair); it is not a biometric reader.
distractors.C: A smart card reader authenticates from a physical card the user inserts/taps, not from a body trait.

explanation.exam_pattern: Unlock 'by touch' / body trait = biometric (fingerprint reader). TPM stores keys; smart card = possession.

questions.stem: A laptop has two SO-DIMM slots and supports dual-channel memory. To give the user 16 GB with the BEST memory bandwidth, how should the technician install it?

options.text: Install the single fastest SO-DIMM available and ignore the second slot
Install two matched 8 GB SO-DIMMs, one in each slot, to enable dual-channel mode
Install a 16 GB and a 4 GB SO-DIMM together
Install one 16 GB SO-DIMM and leave the second slot empty

explanation.correct: Dual-channel needs a matched module in each channel. Two identical 8 GB SO-DIMMs populate both channels, roughly doubling memory bandwidth over a single stick.

distractors.A: A single module — however fast — still runs single-channel; dual-channel requires two populated channels.
distractors.C: Mismatched capacities break symmetric dual-channel (best case a slower flex mode), so it is not optimal.
distractors.D: One 16 GB module fills only one channel, so the system runs in single-channel mode.

explanation.exam_pattern: Best laptop RAM bandwidth = a MATCHED pair, one per channel (dual-channel). One stick = single-channel.

questions.stem: An older laptop uses a CCFL-backlit LCD. One component converts the laptop's low-voltage DC into the high-voltage AC the CCFL tube needs, and its failure is a common cause of a dim or flickering screen. Which component is it?

explanation.correct: The inverter steps the laptop's low-voltage DC up to the high-voltage AC a CCFL backlight tube requires. A failing inverter commonly causes a dim, flickering, or dark screen.

distractors.A: The digitizer senses touch input; it has nothing to do with powering the backlight.
distractors.B: The GPU renders the image but does not supply backlight power.
distractors.D: The polarizer is a passive optical layer in the LCD stack, not a power-conversion component.

explanation.exam_pattern: CCFL backlight needs an inverter (DC->high-voltage AC). Dim/flicker on a CCFL screen -> suspect the inverter.

questions.stem: A newer laptop LCD uses LED backlighting rather than CCFL. Which statement about the LED backlight is ACCURATE?

options.text: It still requires a CCFL inverter to operate
It is more energy-efficient and allows a thinner panel, with no high-voltage inverter required
It removes the need for an LCD layer entirely
Each pixel emits its own light, so the panel needs no backlight at all

explanation.correct: LED backlights are driven directly from low-voltage DC, so they drop the inverter, run cooler and more efficiently, and let panels be thinner than CCFL designs.

distractors.A: The point of LED backlighting is that it needs no high-voltage inverter at all.
distractors.C: An LED-backlit display still uses an LCD layer to form the image; the LEDs only light it.
distractors.D: Per-pixel self-emission describes OLED. An LED-backlit LCD still shines light through a shared backlight and LCD layer.

explanation.exam_pattern: LED-backlit LCD still has a backlight + LCD layer (no inverter). Per-pixel self-lit = OLED.

questions.stem: On a touchscreen laptop the image displays perfectly, but taps and swipes no longer register anywhere on the screen. Which component has MOST likely failed?

explanation.correct: The digitizer is the touch-sensing layer bonded over the display. If touch is dead but the picture is fine, the digitizer (or its cable) is the suspect.

distractors.A: A failed LCD panel would show a bad or missing image — but the stem says the image is perfect.
distractors.C: An inverter powers a CCFL backlight; its failure dims the screen, it does not kill touch input.
distractors.D: A GPU fault corrupts or blanks the rendered image; it does not selectively disable touch while the image is fine.

explanation.exam_pattern: Image good + touch dead = digitizer. Image bad + touch fine = LCD panel.

questions.stem: An executive works on confidential data on flights and wants to stop the passengers beside them from reading the laptop screen. Which accessory BEST addresses this?

explanation.correct: A privacy filter narrows the viewing angle so the screen looks dark to anyone off to the side, blocking shoulder-surfing while staying readable head-on.

distractors.A: An anti-glare protector cuts reflections; it does nothing to hide the screen from a neighbor.
distractors.C: A blue-light filter reduces eye strain and does not restrict who can see the screen.
distractors.D: A webcam cover blocks the camera lens, not the view of the display.

explanation.exam_pattern: Stop side viewing / shoulder-surfing = privacy filter (narrows viewing angle). Anti-glare only cuts reflections.

questions.stem: A graphic designer needs a laptop whose LCD gives the most accurate, consistent color across wide viewing angles. Which LCD panel type should the technician recommend?

explanation.correct: IPS panels are prized for accurate, color-consistent reproduction that holds up across wide viewing angles — the standard pick for color-critical work.

distractors.A: VA panels give strong contrast, but colors shift more off-axis than on an IPS panel.
distractors.B: E-ink is a low-power reflective technology for e-readers, not a color-accurate laptop display.
distractors.C: TN panels are cheap and fast but have the weakest color and narrowest viewing angles.

explanation.exam_pattern: Color accuracy + wide angles among LCDs = IPS. TN = cheap/fast/poor angles; VA = high contrast.

questions.stem: A laptop advertises a Thunderbolt 3 port. Which TWO statements about Thunderbolt 3 are correct? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: It uses a proprietary rectangular connector that is incompatible with USB-C
It can carry PCIe and DisplayPort data over a single cable
It supports speeds up to 40 Gbps
It is limited to 5 Gbps, the same as USB 3.0

explanation.correct: Thunderbolt 3 runs up to 40 Gbps and tunnels both PCIe and DisplayPort over one cable, which is why it can drive docks, external GPUs, and high-res monitors.

distractors.A: Thunderbolt 3 uses the USB-C connector; a USB-C device plugs into a TB3 port (the port is backward-compatible with USB-C).
distractors.D: 5 Gbps is USB 3.0 (USB 3.2 Gen 1). Thunderbolt 3 is eight times that at 40 Gbps.

explanation.exam_pattern: Thunderbolt 3/4 = USB-C connector, up to 40 Gbps, tunnels PCIe + DisplayPort.

questions.stem: At their desk a user wants one connection to the laptop that adds Gigabit Ethernet, drives two external monitors, and delivers charging power — going beyond simply mirroring the laptop's built-in ports. Which accessory is this?

explanation.correct: A docking station adds capabilities the laptop may not have on its own — extra video outputs, wired networking, more ports, and power delivery — through a single connection.

distractors.A: A USB hub only fans out additional USB ports; it does not drive monitors or supply laptop charging.
distractors.C: A KVM switch shares one keyboard, video, and mouse among multiple computers — a different purpose entirely.
distractors.D: A port replicator essentially duplicates the ports the laptop already has; it does not add video outputs or charging beyond that.

explanation.exam_pattern: Adds NEW capabilities (video, Ethernet, charging) = docking station. Just mirrors existing ports = port replicator.

questions.stem: A technician needs a charge-and-sync cable for an older iPhone made before Apple moved to USB-C. Which proprietary connector does that phone use?

explanation.correct: Lightning is Apple's small, reversible proprietary connector used on iPhones (and many iPads) before the switch to USB-C.

distractors.A: Thunderbolt is a high-speed interface (on USB-C connectors), not the iPhone's proprietary charge/sync port.
distractors.C: Micro-USB is the older Android/peripheral connector, never used as the iPhone charge port.
distractors.D: USB-C is the later, industry-standard reversible connector Apple moved to; the stem specifies a device from before that change.

explanation.exam_pattern: Pre-USB-C iPhone charge/sync = Lightning (Apple proprietary).

questions.stem: A user wants to add removable flash storage to an Android phone that has an expansion slot. Which memory card format is designed for that slot?

explanation.correct: microSD is the tiny flash card format built for phones and other small mobile devices; an adapter lets it also fit full-size SD slots.

distractors.A: CompactFlash is a large, thick card used in professional cameras, far too big for a phone slot.
distractors.C: Full-size SD cards are used in cameras and laptops; they do not fit a phone's microSD slot.
distractors.D: MMC is a legacy card format largely superseded by SD/microSD and not used in modern phone slots.

explanation.exam_pattern: Phone removable storage = microSD. Full-size SD = cameras/laptops; CF = pro cameras.

questions.stem: A technician notices a rectangular USB Type-A port on a laptop has a blue plastic insert. By common convention, what does the blue color indicate?

options.text: It is a USB 2.0 Hi-Speed port (480 Mbps)
It supplies no power and is data-only
It is a USB 3.0 (USB 3.2 Gen 1) SuperSpeed port (5 Gbps)

explanation.correct: By convention a blue insert marks a USB 3.0 (USB 3.2 Gen 1) SuperSpeed port rated at 5 Gbps.

distractors.A: USB 2.0 Hi-Speed ports are conventionally black (and run 480 Mbps), not blue.
distractors.B: USB-A ports still provide power; color coding signals speed, not a lack of power.
distractors.D: Thunderbolt uses the USB-C connector, not a blue Type-A port.

explanation.exam_pattern: Blue USB-A insert = USB 3.0 SuperSpeed (5 Gbps); black = USB 2.0 (480 Mbps).

questions.stem: A user with no Wi-Fi wants to get their laptop online through their smartphone's cellular data. Which TWO of the following are valid ways to share that connection? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Connect the phone to the laptop with a USB cable and enable USB tethering
Enable airplane mode on the phone
Hold the phone against the laptop to transfer the connection over NFC
Turn on the phone's Wi-Fi hotspot and join it from the laptop

explanation.correct: USB tethering shares cellular data over the cable (and charges the phone), while a Wi-Fi hotspot broadcasts it as an SSID the laptop joins. (Bluetooth tethering is a third valid method, not listed here.)

distractors.B: Airplane mode disables the phone's radios, which would cut off the cellular data you are trying to share.
distractors.C: NFC works only at a few centimeters for tap-to-pay/tap-to-pair; it does not carry an internet session.

explanation.exam_pattern: Share phone data = USB tethering, Wi-Fi hotspot, or Bluetooth tethering. NFC/airplane mode do not apply.

questions.stem: A flight crew asks a passenger to disable all of their phone's wireless radios at once before takeoff. Which single setting does this?

explanation.correct: Airplane mode turns off the device's radios together — cellular, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and NFC — in one action (Wi-Fi/Bluetooth can be re-enabled separately if allowed).

distractors.A: Disabling Bluetooth alone leaves cellular and Wi-Fi active.
distractors.B: Turning off the hotspot stops sharing data but does not disable the phone's own radios.
distractors.D: Do Not Disturb silences notifications and calls but leaves the radios transmitting.

explanation.exam_pattern: Disable ALL radios at once = airplane mode. Do Not Disturb only silences alerts.

questions.stem: A user cannot get a new Bluetooth speaker to connect to their phone. Which step is specifically required to establish the initial Bluetooth link between the two devices?

options.text: Insert a SIM card into the speaker
Assign the speaker a static IP address
Put the devices in pairing/discoverable mode and confirm the passkey
Join both devices to the same Wi-Fi SSID

explanation.correct: Bluetooth requires pairing: make the accessory discoverable, select it on the phone, and confirm the passkey/PIN so the two devices trust each other.

distractors.A: A SIM identifies a phone to a cellular carrier; a Bluetooth speaker has no SIM.
distractors.B: Bluetooth devices do not use IP addressing; no static IP is involved in pairing.
distractors.D: Bluetooth is its own short-range link and does not depend on sharing a Wi-Fi SSID.

explanation.exam_pattern: Bluetooth = discoverable/pairing mode + confirm passkey. No IP, SSID, or SIM needed.

questions.stem: A hiking app needs precise outdoor positioning even when there is no cellular signal and no nearby Wi-Fi. Which technology provides this?

explanation.correct: GPS receives signals from navigation satellites, so it gives precise location outdoors independent of any cell or Wi-Fi network.

distractors.A: Cellular triangulation needs cell towers in range and is far less precise — exactly what is missing here.
distractors.B: NFC is a few-centimeter tap technology and provides no geographic location at all.
distractors.C: Wi-Fi positioning relies on known nearby access points, which the scenario rules out.

explanation.exam_pattern: Precise location with no cell/Wi-Fi = GPS (satellites). Tower/Wi-Fi methods need that infrastructure.

questions.stem: A user upgrades to a new phone on the same carrier and wants to move their phone number and subscriber identity over by swapping a removable card. Which component stores that subscriber identity?

explanation.correct: The SIM (Subscriber Identity Module) card stores the subscriber identity (IMSI) and carrier credentials, so moving it to a compatible phone carries the service over.

distractors.A: A microSD card holds user files and media; it does not identify the subscriber to the carrier.
distractors.C: The baseband modem processes the cellular radio signal but does not store the subscriber identity.
distractors.D: eMMC is soldered internal storage for the OS and data, not a removable subscriber-identity card.

explanation.exam_pattern: Removable card that identifies you to the carrier = SIM. microSD/eMMC are storage, not identity.

questions.stem: A user reads the same email account on a phone, a tablet, and a laptop and wants messages and folders to stay in sync, remaining stored on the mail server. Which standard retrieval protocol should be configured?

explanation.correct: IMAP keeps mail on the server and syncs read state and folders across every device, which is exactly what multi-device access needs.

distractors.A: SMTP only sends/relays outgoing mail; it does not retrieve or sync a mailbox.
distractors.B: POP3 typically downloads mail to a single device (often removing it from the server) and does not sync folders across devices.
distractors.D: FTP transfers files between hosts and has nothing to do with email retrieval.

explanation.exam_pattern: Multi-device, server-stored, synced mail = IMAP. POP3 = download to one device.

questions.stem: A technician is configuring a mobile mail client to retrieve mail using IMAP secured with SSL/TLS. Which port should the incoming-mail setting use?

explanation.correct: Secure IMAP (IMAP over SSL/TLS, IMAPS) uses TCP port 993.

distractors.B: Port 143 is plain (unencrypted) IMAP.
distractors.C: Port 995 is secure POP3 (POP3S), not IMAP.
distractors.D: Port 110 is unencrypted POP3.

explanation.exam_pattern: IMAP 143 / IMAPS 993; POP3 110 / POP3S 995. 'Secure IMAP' = 993.

questions.stem: Under a BYOD policy, a company must be able to control and remotely wipe ONLY its corporate email and apps on an employee-owned phone, without touching the employee's personal photos and accounts. Which approach BEST meets this requirement?

options.text: Full Mobile Device Management (MDM) enrollment that manages the whole device and wipes it entirely
Mobile Application Management (MAM) that containerizes corporate apps and allows a selective wipe of just that data
Performing a full factory reset whenever an employee leaves

explanation.correct: MAM manages at the application level, placing corporate apps and data in a container the company can configure and selectively wipe while leaving personal data untouched — ideal for BYOD.

distractors.A: Full MDM manages the entire device; a full wipe would also erase the user's personal data, which the policy forbids.
distractors.C: A factory reset erases everything on the device, personal data included — the opposite of selective separation.
distractors.D: Full-device encryption protects data at rest but does not separate or selectively wipe corporate vs personal data.

explanation.exam_pattern: Separate/selectively wipe corporate data on a personal device = MAM (containerization). MDM manages the whole device.

questions.stem: To sign in to a corporate app, a user enters their password and then a one-time code generated by an authenticator app on their phone. What does this describe?

options.text: Multi-factor authentication, where the code adds a second 'something you know' factor
Biometric authentication, a 'something you are' factor
Multi-factor authentication, where the app code adds a 'something you have' factor to the password
Single sign-on (SSO) that replaces the password with one login for many apps

explanation.correct: Using a password plus a code from an authenticator app combines two different factor types: 'something you know' (password) and 'something you have' (the phone/app that generates the code) = MFA.

distractors.A: The one-time code is tied to a device you possess, so it is a 'something you have' factor, not another 'something you know'.
distractors.B: No fingerprint, face, or other body trait is used here, so it is not a biometric ('something you are') factor.
distractors.D: SSO lets one authentication cover many apps; it does not describe adding a second factor at login.

explanation.exam_pattern: Password + authenticator-app code = MFA (know + have). Authenticator/token code = 'something you have'.

questions.stem: A user wants their email to stay stored on the mail server and remain in sync whether they read it from a phone or a laptop. Which protocol, and its default TCP port, supports this server-side mailbox access?

explanation.correct: IMAP (TCP 143) keeps messages on the server and synchronizes mailbox state across multiple devices.

distractors.B: HTTPS (TCP 443) carries secure web traffic (e.g., a webmail front-end), not the mail retrieval protocol itself.
distractors.C: POP3 (TCP 110) typically downloads mail and removes it from the server, so it does not keep multiple devices in sync.
distractors.D: SMTP (TCP 25) sends/relays outbound mail between servers; it does not retrieve a mailbox.

explanation.exam_pattern: IMAP 143 = server-side multi-device sync; POP3 110 = download-and-remove; SMTP 25 = send.

questions.stem: To replace insecure Telnet for remote command-line management of a switch, an administrator enables an encrypted protocol. Which port must the firewall allow?

explanation.correct: SSH uses TCP 22 to provide an encrypted remote command-line session, the secure replacement for Telnet.

distractors.A: TCP 80 is HTTP web traffic, unrelated to remote CLI management.
distractors.B: TCP 23 is Telnet itself — the unencrypted protocol being replaced.
distractors.D: TCP 3389 is RDP, a graphical remote-desktop protocol, not a command-line one.

explanation.exam_pattern: SSH 22 = encrypted CLI; Telnet 23 = plaintext CLI; RDP 3389 = graphical remote desktop.

questions.stem: Classic (active-mode) FTP uses two separate TCP ports by default — one for commands and one for data. Which TWO ports are these? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: FTP uses TCP 21 for the control/command channel and TCP 20 for the active-mode data channel.

distractors.B: TCP 25 is SMTP for outbound email, not file transfer.
distractors.C: TCP 22 is SSH, which also carries SFTP/SCP — a different, encrypted transfer method, not FTP.

explanation.exam_pattern: FTP = TCP 21 (control) + TCP 20 (data); SFTP rides SSH on TCP 22.

questions.stem: Windows file and printer sharing needs to work directly over TCP/IP without legacy NetBIOS. Which port carries this SMB/CIFS traffic?

explanation.correct: SMB/CIFS runs directly over TCP 445 (direct hosting), the modern file- and printer-sharing port.

distractors.A: TCP 143 is IMAP email retrieval.
distractors.C: TCP 389 is LDAP directory lookups.
distractors.D: TCP 139 is the legacy NetBIOS Session Service that older SMB used before direct hosting (part of the 137-139 NetBIOS range).

explanation.exam_pattern: SMB/CIFS direct over TCP 445; NetBIOS 137-139 is the legacy path.

questions.stem: A monitoring server must RECEIVE unsolicited trap notifications sent by SNMP agents on network devices. Which UDP port does the manager listen on for those traps?

explanation.correct: SNMP managers receive agent-initiated traps/informs on UDP 162.

distractors.A: UDP 161 is where the SNMP AGENT listens for the manager's polling (GET/SET) requests — not where traps are received.
distractors.B: UDP 67 is the DHCP server port, unrelated to SNMP.
distractors.C: TCP/UDP 389 is LDAP for directory services, unrelated to SNMP.

explanation.exam_pattern: SNMP agent polled on UDP 161; manager receives traps on UDP 162.

questions.stem: A growing office must segment its network into VLANs and prioritize voice traffic with QoS. Which device supports this configuration?

explanation.correct: A managed switch exposes a configuration interface for VLANs, QoS, port security, and monitoring.

distractors.A: A hub is a Layer 1 repeater that copies signals to all ports with no intelligence at all.
distractors.B: An unmanaged switch is plug-and-play with no VLAN, QoS, or management interface.
distractors.D: An access point bridges wireless clients onto the LAN but does not provide switch VLAN/QoS configuration.

explanation.exam_pattern: Need VLANs/QoS/management = managed switch; plug-and-play with no config = unmanaged.

questions.stem: An existing non-PoE switch must deliver power over Ethernet to a single ceiling access point at the end of one cable run, as cheaply as possible. Which device fits?

explanation.correct: A PoE injector adds power to a single Ethernet link between a non-PoE switch and one powered device — the cheapest fix for one endpoint.

distractors.A: A patch panel only terminates and organizes cabling; it passes no power.
distractors.C: A media converter changes the physical medium (e.g., copper to fiber); it does not supply power.
distractors.D: A PoE switch powers every port but means replacing the whole switch just to power one device.

explanation.exam_pattern: Power one link off a non-PoE switch = PoE injector; power many ports = PoE switch (802.3af ~15 W, 802.3at ~30 W at the port).

questions.stem: An IP phone needs roughly 25 W delivered over its Ethernet cable. Which standard must the switch support to provide that power?

explanation.correct: 802.3at (PoE+) supplies about 30 W at the port (~25.5 W at the device), enough for a 25 W load.

distractors.A: 802.3ad is link aggregation (LACP) — bonding links for bandwidth, not supplying power.
distractors.C: 802.3af (standard PoE) supplies only ~15.4 W at the port (~12.95 W at the device) — not enough.
distractors.D: 802.11ac is a Wi-Fi standard and has nothing to do with power delivery.

explanation.exam_pattern: 802.3af ~15 W, 802.3at (PoE+) ~30 W at the port; a higher draw needs PoE+.

questions.stem: A fiber-to-the-home ISP installs a box where the incoming optical fiber terminates and is converted to an Ethernet handoff for the customer's router. What is this device?

explanation.correct: An ONT terminates the fiber at the premises and converts the optical signal to an electrical/Ethernet handoff.

distractors.A: A cable modem connects over coaxial DOCSIS, not fiber.
distractors.B: A DSL modem connects over twisted-pair telephone lines, not fiber.
distractors.C: A NIC is the network adapter inside a host, not the ISP's fiber demarcation device.

explanation.exam_pattern: Fiber termination/handoff at the premises = ONT; coax = cable modem; phone line = DSL modem.

questions.stem: In which networking approach is the control plane (which makes forwarding decisions) decoupled from the data plane and managed centrally by programmable software?

explanation.correct: SDN separates the control plane from the data plane and centralizes control in programmable software/controllers.

distractors.A: An unmanaged switch forwards frames with no programmable control plane at all.
distractors.B: A patch panel is passive cabling hardware with no planes to separate.
distractors.D: A traditional router keeps the control and data planes together inside each box.

explanation.exam_pattern: Control plane separated from data plane + centrally programmable = SDN.

questions.stem: Which 802.11 wireless standard operates ONLY in the 5 GHz band?

explanation.correct: 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5) operates only in the 5 GHz band and delivers multi-gigabit throughput.

distractors.A: 802.11n is dual-band, working in both 2.4 and 5 GHz (up to 600 Mbps).
distractors.B: 802.11b operates only in 2.4 GHz (up to 11 Mbps).
distractors.D: 802.11g operates only in 2.4 GHz (up to 54 Mbps).

explanation.exam_pattern: a/ac = 5 GHz; b/g = 2.4 GHz; n = both; ac is 5 GHz-only and multi-gigabit.

questions.stem: Three access points cover the same area on the 2.4 GHz band. Which channel assignment avoids overlapping, interfering channels?

explanation.correct: In the 2.4 GHz band, channels 1, 6, and 11 are the standard non-overlapping set (each 20 MHz channel is spaced far enough apart to avoid overlap).

distractors.B: Channels 2, 5, and 9 still overlap and are not the recognized non-overlapping set.
distractors.C: Channels 1, 2, and 3 are adjacent and overlap heavily, so the APs would interfere.
distractors.D: Channel 12 is not usable in North America, and 1/6/12 is not the standard set.

explanation.exam_pattern: 2.4 GHz non-overlapping channels = 1, 6, 11.

questions.stem: A wireless standard reaches theoretical throughput near 9.6 Gbps and, in its 6E variant, adds use of the 6 GHz band. Which standard is this?

explanation.correct: 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) peaks near 9.6 Gbps and works in 2.4 and 5 GHz; the 6E designation adds the 6 GHz band.

distractors.A: 802.11g peaks at 54 Mbps in 2.4 GHz.
distractors.B: 802.11n peaks around 600 Mbps across 2.4/5 GHz.
distractors.D: 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5) is 5 GHz only and tops out well below 9.6 Gbps, with no 6 GHz support.

explanation.exam_pattern: 802.11ax = Wi-Fi 6 (~9.6 Gbps); Wi-Fi 6E adds the 6 GHz band.

questions.stem: A customer taps a smartphone within a few centimeters of a payment terminal to pay. Which short-range wireless technology is in use?

explanation.correct: NFC is a 13.56 MHz technology with a range of only about 4 cm, used for contactless tap-to-pay.

distractors.A: Bluetooth pairs devices over roughly 10 meters — far beyond a tap and not the standard here.
distractors.B: Infrared needs line of sight and is used for legacy remotes/data links, not payments.
distractors.D: General/active RFID can be read from centimeters to meters; NFC is the specific ~4 cm, tap-to-pay branch of RFID.

explanation.exam_pattern: Tap-to-pay at ~4 cm = NFC (a 13.56 MHz, very-short-range form of RFID).

questions.stem: A company links two buildings about 3 km apart using directional antennas with clear line of sight, instead of trenching cable. Which wireless solution is this?

options.text: A single omnidirectional 2.4 GHz access point

explanation.correct: Long-range fixed wireless uses directional (point-to-point) antennas with line of sight to bridge sites kilometers apart.

distractors.A: NFC works only within a few centimeters.
distractors.B: Bluetooth is a personal-area technology effective for only about 10 meters.
distractors.C: A single omnidirectional AP radiates in all directions over a small area and cannot bridge a multi-kilometer point-to-point link.

explanation.exam_pattern: Multi-kilometer point-to-point with directional antennas + line of sight = long-range fixed wireless.

questions.stem: A company routes all employee web requests through a server that caches frequently visited pages and blocks access to disallowed sites. Which server role is this?

explanation.correct: A proxy server sits between clients and the internet to cache content and filter/allow outbound web access.

distractors.A: A DNS server resolves names to IP addresses.
distractors.B: A print server manages shared printers.
distractors.D: A load balancer spreads incoming traffic across multiple back-end servers; it is not for caching or filtering user web access.

explanation.exam_pattern: Caches + filters outbound user web traffic = proxy server.

questions.stem: A popular website runs on a farm of identical web servers. Which device distributes incoming client requests across those servers so no single one is overwhelmed?

explanation.correct: A load balancer distributes inbound requests across a pool of identical servers for capacity and availability.

distractors.B: A proxy forwards and filters outbound client requests; it is not for distributing inbound load across a server pool.
distractors.C: A spam gateway filters inbound email for junk and malware.
distractors.D: A DHCP server leases IP configuration to clients.

explanation.exam_pattern: Spreads inbound load across many identical servers = load balancer.

questions.stem: A network administrator wants routers, switches, and firewalls to forward their event logs to one central collector for retention and review. Which server role does this?

explanation.correct: A syslog server centrally collects and stores event/log messages forwarded by network devices.

distractors.A: A file server stores user files and shares, not device event logs specifically.
distractors.B: A spam gateway filters inbound email.
distractors.D: An authentication server validates credentials (e.g., RADIUS/Active Directory); it is not a log collector.

explanation.exam_pattern: Centralized collection of device event logs = syslog server.

questions.stem: A utility uses a specialized system to supervise and collect data from remote industrial equipment such as pumps and sensors across a facility. This system is BEST described as?

explanation.correct: SCADA (supervisory control and data acquisition) monitors and controls industrial processes and equipment as part of an ICS.

distractors.B: A proxy server forwards and filters web requests.
distractors.C: A load balancer distributes network traffic across servers.
distractors.D: UTM is an all-in-one security appliance, not an industrial control/monitoring system.

explanation.exam_pattern: Supervisory control + data acquisition for industrial/ICS equipment = SCADA.

questions.stem: Which TWO of the following are security appliances whose main purpose is to inspect or filter traffic, rather than general-purpose server roles? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: A UTM combines multiple security functions (firewall, IPS, antivirus, content filtering) in one appliance, and a spam gateway inspects/filters inbound email — both are security appliances that filter traffic.

distractors.B: A file server stores and serves files; it is not a security-filtering device.
distractors.D: A print server shares printers; it performs no traffic inspection or filtering.

explanation.exam_pattern: UTM (multi-function security) and spam gateway (email filtering) are security appliances, not general server roles.

questions.stem: A remote research cabin has no wired service and connects to the internet through a dish aimed at an orbiting satellite. Users notice a long delay on video calls. Which connection type is this?

explanation.correct: Satellite reaches remote sites via a dish to an orbiting satellite, but the long signal path adds high latency — exactly the delay described.

distractors.A: DSL uses twisted-pair phone lines, which are also wired.
distractors.B: Cable uses coaxial DOCSIS over a wired plant, not a satellite.
distractors.C: Fiber is a wired optical service with very low latency, not a dish link.

explanation.exam_pattern: Dish to orbit + high latency + remote availability = satellite.

questions.stem: A home uses existing twisted-pair telephone wiring for internet, and the ISP warns that throughput drops the farther the home is from the provider's central office. Which connection type is this?
